learning_outcomes.text: Discover the electromechanical drives sector, elementary operating principles, and characteristics.
Understand the operation and formulate the mathematical model of direct current drives.
Understand the operation and formulate the mathematical model of synchronous drives.
Understand the operation and formulate the mathematical model of induction drives.
Know the state of the art in drives, related industries, and manufacturers, etc.
Know the different technologies for generating forces, of any type and especially of electromagnetic origin.
Analyze in detail the different types of drives, their electromagnetic structures, the types of power supply, and control.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Industrial applications of magnetic and electromechanical devices
Topic 2: Applied magnetism and magnetic materials
Topic 3: Fundamentals of magnetic and electromechanical devices
teaching_methods: Lectures (participatory, conferences, company visits, fair attendance)
Participatory classes (case resolution, role-playing, application exercises, presentations, debates)
Individual study (readings, exam preparation, exercises, class preparation)

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests, development, short answers, conceptual maps, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of written tests (50%), numerical problem solving (25%), and practice reports (25%). Theoretical and classroom practical content can be assessed via continuous evaluation (partial tests) or a single final exam, both contributing 50% to the final grade. The course is passed with a final grade of 5 or higher, provided no partial grade (theoretical content and practicals) is below 4 points. Late submissions for reports and problems will incur a 20% penalty. Violation of exam rules will result in expulsion and require taking the extraordinary exam for 100% of the course grade.
